sim.title: Where the numbers come from

items.building: Model building — {floors}-story office, about {gfa} m² gross floor area
items.load: Electric load — median energy use intensity for offices in Korea's central region, {eui} kWh/m²·yr (MOLIT 2024 building energy statistics), spread over a weekday hourly profile; peak about {peak} kW. Assumes all energy is electric.
items.solar: Solar — {kwp} kWp on the roof, at Korea's average {hours} generation hours a day (about {daily} kWh/day)
items.ess: ESS — {essKw} kW / {essKwh} kWh, {rte}% round-trip efficiency (NREL ATB). Charges off-peak (22:00–08:00), discharges to cut the daytime peak by {cut}% (the low end of Peak ESS's 15–30% demand-charge savings) and during the 18:00–21:00 peak tariff
items.heatPump: Heat pump — air-source, COP {cop} (KS test case). HVAC assumed at {hvac}% of building load
items.ai: AI savings — about {ai}% energy cost reduction stated for Ninewatt Opti
items.bems: BEMS alerts — example scenes that show real BEMS features (out-of-range alerts and AI analysis): a near-new monthly peak by day and +{pct}% standby power on floor {floor} at night. Time slows down during these scenes.

sim.note: This is a simulation, not measured data. One weekday is compressed into {sec} seconds.

detail.footnote: Simulated values. See 'Simulation basis' at the top right for sources.

ess.title: ESS
ess.peakNote: Charges during off-peak night hours and discharges at the daytime peak. Daily peak demand is {before} kW without the ESS and {after} kW with it (−{cut}%).
ess.socChart: State of charge over the day (%)
ess.powerChart: Charge and discharge over the day (kW)

hp.title: HVAC heat pumps
hp.note: Each 1 kW of electricity makes {cop} kW of heat (COP {cop}). Fan speed follows the HVAC load.
hp.chart: Power use and heat output over the day (kW)

solar.title: Solar generation
solar.note: Solar is covering {share}% of the building load right now.

load.title: Building power
load.note: AI analyzes each floor and trims the busiest floors first, by up to {ai}%. Grid draw drops by what solar and the ESS supply.
load.chart: Building load and grid draw over the day (kW)

bems.title: Ninewatt BEMS
bems.statusOkText: Meter readings are being monitored in real time. An alert goes out as soon as a value leaves its set range.

peak.alert: Close to a new monthly peak of {peak} kW · now {now} kW
peak.ai: HVAC units are starting together, so a peak is expected around 3 pm. The ESS discharges to hold grid draw under {peak} kW.
peak.resolved: Grid {grid} kW · peak held at {peak} kW, no new demand charge

night.alert: Floor {floor} night standby {now} kW · +{pct}% above normal
night.ai: Meeting-room lights and HVAC on floor {floor} stayed on after 10 pm. Schedule-based auto shut-off is recommended.
night.resolved: Floor {floor} standby back to normal ({now} kW)

bems.f1: Shows meter readings in real time and sends an alert automatically when a value leaves its range or set point.
bems.f2: AI explains key changes and what needs checking, based on on-site data.
bems.f3: Build dashboards from the metrics you need, compare periods, and export reports.

gr.title: Insulation · Windows · Shading

scan.title: Thermal scan
scan.desc: First, find where heat escapes. Slab edges (thermal bridges) and window frames show up hottest.

insulation.title: External insulation
insulation.desc: Wrap the floor bands and the wall below each window in insulation panels from outside to close the heat leaks.

windows.title: High-performance windows
windows.desc: Switch to Low-E double glazing with insulated frames to cut heat flowing through the glass.

shading.title: External shading
shading.desc: Louvers above the windows tilt with the sun's height to control incoming sunlight.

gr.note: Finished sections cool down in the thermal view. Simulate the savings for a real building with its own data in GreenPlanner.
gr.footnote: An illustrative scene showing the installation order. Thermal colors are for explanation, not measurements.
